## Document: README.md (Overview)

# @actdim/livestruct-demo

> **Interactive Showcase & Laboratory for @actdim/livestruct, @actdim/msgmesh, and Local-First SQLite OPFS Living Documents**

[![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-live-brightgreen.svg)](https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/demo/)
[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.9+-blue.svg)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)

---

## 1. Purpose of the Showcase

While `@actdim/dynstruct` provides UI component models and `@actdim/msgmesh` provides asynchronous communication, **`@actdim/livestruct`** transforms local-first storage into a living, synchronized document.

This demonstration application showcases the critical differences between in-memory message streaming and durable storage commits:

1. **Separation of Concerns:** 60fps mouse drag operations stream exclusively in RAM over `MsgMesh`, while final state updates commit once to SQLite OPFS.
2. **Zero-Server Multi-Tab Replication:** Mutating properties in one tab synchronizes with all other tabs via `BroadcastChannel` and OPFS without a backend server.
3. **Decoupled Architecture:** UI components interact with documents and the message mesh through strict contracts, avoiding tight coupling to database drivers.
4. **Time-Travel & File Portability:** Integrated Undo/Redo history via event-sourcing and direct export/import of the SQLite project database.

---

## 2. Interactive Zones

The application layout is structured into three coordinated viewports:

```
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+
| ZONE 1: Interactive Canvas         | ZONE 2: LiveDocument Inspector     |
| (2D HTML5 Canvas / Vector Sheet)   | (Dynstruct Reactive Property Form) |
|                                    |                                    |
| - CAD Primitive (Rectangle/Part)   | - Part Name (text input)           |
| - Vertices / Transform Handles     | - Layer Selection (dropdown)       |
| - Interactive Drag & Rotation      | - Fill Color (color picker)        |
| - Real-time Coordinate Display     | - Bounding Box (X, Y, Width, H)    |
| - In-Memory Drag Stream (60fps)    | - Undo / Redo Controls (Ctrl+Z/Y)  |
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+
| ZONE 3: Telemetry & Protocol Monitor (Bus Traffic & Storage Engine Log) |
|                                                                         |
| [RAM] MsgMesh Stream: cad.cursor.drag (60fps, 0 disk I/O)               |
| [DISK] LiveStruct Commit: json_patch transaction in SQLite (OPFS)       |
| [CDC] MsgMesh-Store Broadcast: STORE.ENTITY_PATCHED across tabs         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

## 3. Key Scenarios Demonstrated

### Scenario A: Ephemeral Drag vs Durable Commit
- **Interaction:** Dragging a primitive on the canvas.
- **Data Flow:** Coordinates stream at 60fps via MsgMesh channel `cad.cursor.drag` (green telemetry badge, 0 disk I/O).
- **Commit:** On `mouseUp`, a single `doc.patch()` transaction commits final coordinates to SQLite OPFS (blue telemetry badge).

### Scenario B: Split-View Simulation via Isolated iframes
- **Interaction:** Clicking "Simulate Dual Tab" renders two isolated same-origin `<iframe>` instances side-by-side.
- **Verification:** Because each iframe possesses an independent JavaScript heap, DOM tree, and window context, the synchronization between them proves genuine local-first coordination over `BroadcastChannel` and OPFS without shared in-memory state.
- **Single-Screen & Mobile:** Users witness real multi-window synchronization immediately on a single monitor or mobile device without opening separate browser tabs.

### Scenario C: Project File Export and Import
- **Export:** Clicking "Download Project (.cad)" streams the SQLite binary file directly from OPFS.
- **Import:** Dropping an existing `.cad` SQLite database loads all entities and restores undo/redo history.

---

## 4. Development & Running

```bash
# Start development server
pnpm dev

# Build production bundle
pnpm build

# Run unit tests
pnpm test
```

## Project specifics

<!-- BEGIN ALONG-RULES -->
See the following engineering guidelines:
- `[languages/typescript.md](.along/rules/languages/typescript.md)`
- `[platforms/web.md](.along/rules/platforms/web.md)`
<!-- END ALONG-RULES -->

- **What it is**: Vite + React 19 SPA showcasing `@actdim/livestruct` (LiveStore SQLite in OPFS via `src/livestore/worker.ts` plus the adapter-web shared worker) and `@actdim/msgmesh`; one CAD document `cad_documents/doc-default` driven by `src/cad/store.ts` (`CadStore`). Not published to npm.
- **Commands**: `pnpm dev` (port 4173), `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (Vitest in Node, in-memory store), `pnpm typecheck`; inside mempart run them from `src/` with `pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo <script>`.
- **Entry modes**: `?split=dual` (two isolated same-origin iframes), `?viewport=A|B|native` (child viewport), `?spike=livestore` (raw LiveStore benchmark).
- **Location and workspace**: `demo/` of the livestruct repository (mempart: `src/packages/livestruct/demo`). `@actdim/livestruct` is `workspace:*`; outside mempart the livestruct `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (packages `.` and `demo`, catalog) links it, and `msgmesh` / `utico` come from npm.
- **CI/Pages**: the livestruct `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds the library, then the demo with `DEMO_BASE=/livestruct/demo/`, and deploys it next to the docs at https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/demo/ (step is `continue-on-error` until the `@actdim` siblings 1.12.x are on npm).
- **Knowledge base**: start at `docs/INDEX.md` (architecture, domain model, setup and workflow); library internals live on the livestruct and msgmesh-store sites.
- **Versioning**: the version is unified across the mempart monorepo; change it only via `pnpm run version:sync <version>` from mempart `src/`, never in this `package.json` alone.

# Along Protocol Reference

The managed block in `AGENTS.md` is the always-loaded core of the ALONG-PROTOCOL: where state lives, how work is anchored to an issue, and the list of gates. This article carries the situational procedure the core points to. Pull the section you need with `/along-kb-search` instead of reading the whole file. `along init` and `along update` regenerate this file from the installed protocol; repository-specific guidance belongs in its own `docs/topic--<slug>.md` article or in `AGENTS.md` "Project specifics".

## Scope, Precedence & Subproject Placement

- **Nearest Context Boundary**: Any folder may carry its own `AGENTS.md` + `.along/`; use the NEAREST ones for the area you're working in. On conflict, the more specific wins.
- **Subproject Localization** [gate: subproject-boundary]: In submodules, nested repos or symlinked folders: all entities (issues, sessions, ADRs, history) MUST be created in the NEAREST `.along/`. Agents are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN from dumping subproject changes into the workspace root `.along/`.
- **Multi-Subproject Work** [gate: subproject-boundary]: A change spanning subprojects needs an issue in each touched `.along/`, or a root umbrella issue whose child issues there carry `parent: <umbrella key>`. Edits under a subproject `.along/` are checked by path.
- **Subproject Boundary**: only a nested `.git` or a user-run `along init` makes a subproject; never init a manifest folder.
- **Precedence**: Nearest `.along/` > higher-level `.along/` > global config (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.gemini/config/GEMINI.md`).

## Session Start

Use the NEAREST `.along/` for the area you're working in (fall back to a higher-level one if the folder has none). These files are NOT auto-loaded; read them yourself:

1. `AGENTS.md` (nearest) - conventions to follow.
2. `.along/ISSUES.md` - active issue board (or query `/along-kb-search`).
3. `.along/CONSTRAINTS.md` - active architectural constraints (or full log in `.along/DECISIONS.md` / `.along/DECISIONS/`).
4. Active Issue file `.along/ISSUES/<type>--<slug>.md` for your task.

Also, when relevant: `.along/VISION.md`, `.along/GLOSSARY.md`. These reflect the state WHEN WRITTEN - verify any named file/API/flag against the real code first.

## Multi-Agent & Multi-Branch Concurrency

- **Zero-Manual-Merge Rule** [gate: projection-protection]: On merge conflicts in derived projections (`ISSUES.md`, `INDEX.md`, `DECISIONS.md`), accept either side and run `/along-issue-sync`, `/along-kb-sync`, or `/along-decision-sync` to recompile. `along git setup` registers merge drivers that do this automatically; afterwards run `along git sync`.
- **Append-Only Merge Driver**: `.along/HISTORY.md` and legacy monolithic `.along/DECISIONS.md` are append-only. Configure `.gitattributes` with `merge=union`. Modular ADR files in `.along/DECISIONS/` are isolated per-file to eliminate merge collisions.
- **Untracked Exports** [gate: untracked-exports]: `.along/dashboard.html`, `.along/DASHBOARD.md` and per-machine `.along/diagnostics/` stay out of Git.
- **Context Isolation**: Context is localized to the target issue file, session-scoped blackboard (`.along/.session/<slug>/`), and completed session logs.
- **Parallel Closeout**: `along session list`; on the user's yes `along plan approve --closeout --ready`, then `along session close --ready`.

## Issue Anchoring & Commits

- **No Code Without Issue** [gate: require-active-issue]: Before modifying source code, agents MUST identify or create an issue in `.along/ISSUES/<type>--<slug>.md` and set `status: in-progress`.
- **Session Binding & Plan Approval** [gate: require-plan-approval]: `along start <slug>` binds THIS agent session to the issue; parallel sessions keep their own bindings. Source edits unlock after the user approves the plan (`EnterPlanMode` -> `ExitPlanMode`; outside plan mode, write the plan to a file and run `along plan approve --plan-file <path>` after the user's explicit yes). `along plan status` shows the binding.
- **Exemptions**: Read-only Q&A and 1-line micro-edits (typo fixes, comments) do not require issues.
- **Inquiry Read-Only Invariance (Zero-Mutation Rule on Questions)** [gate: require-plan-approval]: On interrogative prompts ("is X done?", "why did Y fail?"), write/modify tools are STRICTLY PROHIBITED. Return a read-only audit report and ask for confirmation before modifying anything.
- **Commit Binding** [gate: commit-issue-binding]: Every commit via `/along-commit` MUST bind to the active issue slug.
- **No AI Co-Authors**: Commit messages MUST NOT carry `Co-Authored-By:` trailers naming an AI agent (GitHub lists the vendor as a contributor). `along hook install` turns runtime attribution off; opt out via `.along/config.json` `commits.allow_ai_coauthor: true`.

## Issue Plans & Approving Ahead

- **Plan location**: An issue's plan lives next to its ticket in `.along/ISSUES/<key>/plan.md` (committed; moves with the ticket to `done/` and on rename). It is one living file: the approved baseline, then each correction appended as `## Revision N (date, source)` with a `Reason:` line. `along-team` writes its Living Plan there too; blackboards without an issue keep `.along/.session/<slug>/plan.md`.
- **Plan status** (ticket front-matter `plan_status`, shown on the board): `needs-approval` (written, waiting for the user), `approved` (ready to run), `needs-rework` (cannot be followed within the ticket). Agents may set `needs-approval` / `needs-rework`; only `along plan approve`, after the user's explicit yes, sets `approved` [gate: require-plan-approval]: a file-tool edit that sets it is denied, a shell write is reported at Stop.
- **Plan Approval Integrity & Revocation** [gate: require-plan-approval]: Approval records (`.along/.session/*/state.json`, `.along/.session/bindings/*.json`, `.along/.session/*/events.jsonl`, `.along/diagnostics/activity/**`) are strictly protected from modification. Direct writes via file tools or inline shell writers (redirects, `tee`, PowerShell cmdlets, `sed -i`, interpreter one-liners) are denied before execution. Any forged plan approval appearing during a turn without a corresponding ledger `approve` entry is automatically revoked at Stop, returned to `planning` phase, recorded as a gate denial, and reported to the operator.
- **Autonomous Profile & Escalation Policy**:
  - The `autonomous` profile is strictly operator-environment-sourced (`ALONG_PROFILE=autonomous` or `ALONG_AUTONOMOUS=1`). Configuration files (`.along/config.json`), session state, bindings, and hook payloads cannot activate it; `along start --profile autonomous` exits with code 2.
  - Escalation approvals never override a denial from any other gate (containment, CLI safety, test verification, plan approval, etc.). An escalation approval can only permit an action that would otherwise be rejected solely because it is in the escalation-required operations list (e.g. default branch pushes, release creation, tag updates).
  - Escalation checks only run on `PreToolUse`.
  - Architect self-approval in multi-agent orchestration requires explicit operator opt-in via `ALONG_ARCHITECT_SELF_APPROVAL=1`; otherwise the orchestrator marks `plan_status: needs-approval`, transitions status to `needs-input`, and halts for operator review.
- **Approve ahead**: Write the plan (plan mode, or a file), show it, and after the user's yes run `along plan approve <slug>` (`--plan-file <path>` outside plan mode) before `along start`. The issue is not started; the ticket says `plan_status: approved` and the CLI logs the approval in `.along/.session/plan-approvals.jsonl` (machine-local, closed to file tools). A later `along start <slug>`, by the user, the agent, or the orchestrator / runner daemon, runs the plan with no second approval and no re-planning (the orchestrator skips its architect).
- **Approved elsewhere**: `approved` in the ticket with no approval logged on this machine (approved on another machine, or written by hand) is not trusted: show the plan and ask once in the current channel (chat, or the daemon's Telegram reply); the orchestrator stops with `needs-input`.
- **Plans change during work; escalate only past the ticket**: Once approved, the plan belongs to the agents. A deviation they can resolve while still meeting the ticket's requirements and acceptance criteria is resolved on the spot and recorded (`along plan revise <slug> --plan-file <path> --reason "..."`); no one is asked and the status stays `approved`. Only a problem the ticket cannot absorb (a requirement cannot be met or must change, a decision only the user can make) goes to the user: `along plan rework <slug> --reason "..."`, stop, ask. In `along-team`, implementer and reviewer report plan problems to the supervisor, the architect revises, and only a ticket-level problem halts the run. Plans are not checked for staleness: a plan stays valid until the work shows otherwise.

## Entity Ecosystem

- **Entity types**: Issues (`feat`, `bug`, `debt`, `task`, `docs`, `spike`), Decisions (ADRs), Milestones, Sessions. A risk or blocker is an issue tagged `risk`; a spike is a `spike--<slug>` issue with an `## Outcome` section. Full YAML schemas: `docs/topic--domain-model.md`.
- **Canonical keys**: `<type>--<slug>` (e.g. `feat--token-refresh`). Reference by key, NEVER by file path.
- **ADRs**: Modular records in `.along/DECISIONS/ADR-YYYY-MM-DD--<slug>.md` (with legacy fallback to monolithic `DECISIONS.md`). Never edit past entries - mark superseded. Recompile projections (`.along/DECISIONS.md` board and `.along/CONSTRAINTS.md`) via `/along-decision-sync` or `along decision sync`. Create new ADRs via `/along-decision-sync` or `along decision create <slug> --title "..."`. Add terms to `.along/GLOSSARY.md`.
- **Issue lifecycle** [gate: issue-lifecycle]: Complete active issues via `along wrap <slug>` (or `along issue done <slug> --status cancelled|superseded`). Closing as done requires `validate_issue_completion` (no scaffold placeholders, mandatory Acceptance Criteria, all `- [x]` closed).
- **Entity references** [gate: entity-reference-integrity] [gate: entity-deletion-protection]: Never delete an entity other entities reference; use `along issue rename` / `along issue supersede`.
- **Auto-entity creation**: Agents MUST automatically detect user intent (build/fix/refactor -> Issue, blocked/rate-limit -> Issue tagged `risk`, compare/benchmark -> `spike` Issue, release/sprint -> Milestone) and create entities without prompting the user.

## Knowledge Base & Documentation

- **Stable Entry Point**: `README.md` and `docs/` never link into `.along/`; route through `docs/INDEX.md` or `docs/topic--<slug>.md`.
- **Portable Links**: Relative Markdown links only.
- **Fact Grounding**: Agents MUST extract facts from actual code, `README.md`, `docs/`, and `package.json`. Generic LLM placeholders are strictly prohibited.
- **Fast Retrieval**: Agents SHOULD query `/along-kb-search` before reading whole documentation files.
- **Doc Blast Radius**: After non-trivial code changes, agents MUST map affected symbols to `docs/topic--*.md` articles and update them before completing the task.
- **Manual Document Lock** [gate: doc-manual-lock]: Documents marked with `write_policy: manual` (or `locked: true`) are protected from automated agent modification during blast radius sweeps. Modifications require an explicit documentation issue (`docs--<slug>`).
- **Managed Rule Packs** [gate: rule-pack-protection]: Never edit `.along/rules/**/*.md`; `along rules attach` owns them. Project guidelines go to `docs/topic--<slug>.md` or "Project specifics"; revert with `along rules restore`. `.along/rules/gates.yaml` and `.along/scripts/` stay repo-owned.

### Documentation Routing Tree

[gate: doc-routing-compliance]

- Architectural choice / trade-off -> `.along/DECISIONS/` (ADR)
- Public overview / pitch / landing page -> `README.md`
- Technical interface contract / CLI spec -> `docs/topic--<slug>.md` (`type: reference`)
- Conceptual explanation / comparison / philosophy -> `docs/topic--<slug>.md` (`type: explanation`, `write_policy: manual`)
- Procedural walkthrough / runbook -> `docs/topic--<slug>.md` (`type: guide`)

## While Working

- **Token hygiene**: Use quiet flags (`pytest -q`, `dotnet test -v q`), filter outputs, inspect targeted line ranges.
- **Lifecycle hooks first**: Agents MUST use `/along-test`, `/along-build`, `/along-dev` (or `.along/scripts/*.py`) before raw shell commands.
- **Post-change review**: Agents MUST inspect diffs and evaluate blast radius via `along graph-impact` (or static search fallback). Silent skips are forbidden.

## Stage & Session Completion Checklist

When a stage or session completes, agents MUST execute in this order:
1. [ ] **Tests** [gate: test_before_stop]: Run via `/along-test` with quiet flags. Zero failures caused by this issue. On a failure the test gate prints a `[Baseline]` line. Pre-existing failures (red at HEAD, code the issue did not touch): halt, report the exact failures to the user, file an issue, and only with their agreement bypass: `along commit -n --reason "pre-existing failure in <suite>, tracked in <key>"`, `along wrap <slug> -n --reason "..."`. Never edit tests or fixtures to make them pass unless the issue is about them.
2. [ ] **File Integrity**: `git status -u` - all new/modified files non-zero size, no empty placeholders.
3. [ ] **Code Review**: Inspect diff for side effects, verify REQ-N coverage, evaluate blast radius via `along graph-impact` (or static search), verify architectural decision compliance.
4. [ ] **Entity Reconciliation**: Close issues (`done` + move to `done/`), update milestones, record the `## Outcome` of a spike. [gate: unresolved_gate_denial]: every tool call a gate denied is redone within the gate's rules or disclosed (`along gates denials`, `along gates ack <id> --note "..."`); `along wrap` / `along issue done` refuse until the user has replied to a disclosure (`--force-reason` after their reply).
5. [ ] **Doc Blast Radius**: Update affected `docs/topic--*.md`, `README.md` and Project specifics; add new terms to `.along/GLOSSARY.md` (create it on first use); touch `.along/VISION.md` only if scope/roadmap changed; run `/along-kb-sync`.
6. [ ] **Session Log & Wrap** [gate: wrap_before_stop]: `along wrap <slug> --summary "<summary>" (--decisions <ADR...> | --no-decisions)` writes `.along/SESSIONS/<YYYY>/<date>--<slug>.md` (summary, decisions, attributed `files:`, blackboard record), compiles projections, and appends to `.along/HISTORY.md` (provide `--summary` or let it fallback to issue title).
7. [ ] **Projections** [gate: projection_sync_before_stop]: Run `/along-issue-sync` and `/along-decision-sync`.
8. [ ] **HISTORY**: Verify line in `.along/HISTORY.md` (appended automatically by `along wrap`; update via `along history append <slug> "..."` if needed).
9. [ ] **Compaction**: Advise user to run `/compact`.

## Multi-Agent Routing

- **Mandatory Adaptive Complexity Escalation & Execution Mode Routing**: When scope touches > 3 files, crosses subsystems, or refactors core engines: single-agent execution is forbidden - route to `along-team`. Plans MUST declare `Execution Mode: Direct` or `Role-Based`. Role-based blackboards (`along scratch init`) are held to the step loop [gate: team-step-active] [gate: team-reviews-before-stop]; dropping it needs `along scratch fallback <slug> --reason "..."`.

## Tool-Use Rules

- **Contract-First Lifecycle**:
  - Agents MUST execute `.along/scripts/<action>.py` or `/along-test`, `/along-build`, `/along-dev` before raw shell commands.
  - When `.along/scripts/` is missing, `along test`/`along build` auto-detects and synthesizes hooks.
  - In submodules, execute the hook from that subproject's own `.along/scripts/`.
- **Environment Isolation**:
  - Agents MUST NOT install system-wide or global packages when a script fails. Fix the architecture (missing `bootstrap.ensure_deps()`, incorrect `uv` wrapper), not the environment.
- **Workspace Containment** [gate: workspace-containment]: Read and write only inside the workspace. Writes elsewhere are limited to the temp dir and runtime artifact dirs. Other repos need `allowed_roots` (`.along/rules/gates.yaml`, issue frontmatter, `along start --allow-root`). Never touch credential stores (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`).
- **Runtimes Without Along Hooks** (Claude Cowork, Cursor, OpenCode, plain shells): gates are advisory there. Agents MUST self-apply every gate-tagged rule and use the `along` CLI for tests, commits, entity changes, and wrap instead of raw tools. `along doctor` reports the enforcement level.
- **File Modification & Anti-Deletion**:
  - Never delete, truncate, or overwrite existing documentation, comments, or code unless explicitly instructed.
  - After batch edits or migrations, agents MUST run `git diff --stat` and inspect unexpected size reductions.
  - No stubs or skeletons in place of populated code.
  - Anchor edits on minimal unique chunks. Restore unintended deletions immediately.
- **Clean ASCII**: ASCII punctuation only (no typographic dashes, quotes, ellipsis, bullets, NBSP/zero-width chars or BOM); `along sanitize --write` fixes them.
- **Markdown**: Every code fence names a language.
- **Commit-time checks**: typography, code fences, links, filenames, secrets, stubs and AI co-authors are checked by `along lint` (pre-commit and CI), not while you work.
- **Bypass Is The User's Call**: `-n`, `--force-reason`, `scratch fallback` need `--reason` and the user's reply after the failure; each bypass is recorded (`along gates stats`).
- **File Content Via Tools Only** [gate: cli_safety]: Create/edit files with the agent's file tools. NEVER carry content in heredocs, `python -c`, or inline shell. Write scripts to a file first.
- **No Ad-Hoc Shell Code Probing**: Agents must never use `python -c` or inline shell commands to probe internal module symbols or inspect functions. Internal engine packages (`alongkit`, `scripts`) are not installed into the global Python environment, and ad-hoc shell probing produces confusing error traces instead of actionable information. Prescribed inspection tools: static file tools (`view_file`, `grep_search`), AST tools (`along graph-*`), official CLI subcommands (`along <command> --help`), or dedicated hermetic tests in `tests/`.
- **CLI Black-Box Invariance**: Agents MUST treat the Along CLI and development tools as strict opaque black-box executables. Reading Along engine source code (`.along/bin/*.py`, `~/.along/bin/`, `alongkit/**`, `along_*.py`) to inspect internals, arguments, or data structures is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN unless working on the Along repository itself. Always use `along <command> --help` or official documentation in `docs/`. If an Along command returns an error or fails validation, report the exact CLI error output to the user immediately. Do not attempt to reverse-engineer or debug the Along engine.
- **Verify Written Files**: After writing/patching, confirm parsing (`python -m compileall -q`, `bash -n`, etc.) before moving on.
- **Hermetic Tests**: Tests MUST target throwaway fixtures (`tempfile.mkdtemp()`), never the live repository. Read-only access to live state is allowed. Keep a meta-test that verifies `git status --porcelain -u` stays clean.
- Windows-safe filenames: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, date first.
- Keep `ISSUES.md` compact: `along context-budget --check` enforces the limit.
- Never write secrets into tracked files.

---

## Document: docs/topic--architecture.md (System Architecture & Flow)

# @actdim/livestruct-demo Architecture

## 1. System Overview

`@actdim/livestruct-demo` is a Vite + React 19 single-page app that showcases `@actdim/livestruct` living documents on top of LiveStore (SQLite in OPFS, run in a dedicated worker plus a shared worker) and a typed `@actdim/msgmesh` bus. One CAD document (`doc-default` in collection `cad_documents`) is edited from a 2D canvas and a property inspector; a telemetry monitor shows which changes stay in RAM and which reach SQLite.

The libraries themselves are documented on their own sites; this topic only covers how the demo wires them:

- livestruct: [https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/](https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/)
- msgmesh-store: [https://actdim.github.io/msgmesh-store/](https://actdim.github.io/msgmesh-store/)

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  App.tsx (query params: spike / viewport / split)                             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Zone 1: VectorCanvas        |  Zone 2: PropertyInspector (MobX observer)     |
|  pointer drag -> doc.patch   |  field edits -> CadStore.updateShapeProperties |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  SplitSimulator: single | dual iframe (?viewport=A/B) | native tab            |
|  undo/redo hotkeys, export (.cad download), import (file picker / drop)       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Zone 3: TelemetryMonitor: liveStore.events$ + bus channel cad.cursor.drag    |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  cad/store.ts  CadStore = LiveStoreInstance + LiveCollection + LiveDocument   |
|                + MsgBus<CadMsgStruct> + undo/redo snapshot stacks             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  @actdim/livestruct  (commit scheduler, BroadcastChannel overlay channel)     |
|  LiveStore adapter-web: livestore/worker.ts + shared worker -> SQLite (OPFS)  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## 2. Core Components

| Component | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `App` | `src/App.tsx` | Reads `spike`, `viewport`, `split` query params, creates one `CadStore` per browsing context, exposes it as `window.__cadStore`, renders the host shell or a child viewport. |
| `CadStore` / `initCadStore` | `src/cad/store.ts` | Creates the LiveStruct store (`name: 'cad_store'`, unique `sessionId` per context), the `cad_documents` collection and the `doc-default` document seeded with `DEFAULT_SHAPES`; counts `commit`, `overlay_sent`, `overlay_received`, `local_patch` events; keeps undo/redo stacks. |
| LiveStore worker | `src/livestore/worker.ts` | `makeWorker({ schema })` with the schema exported by `@actdim/livestruct/engine`; loaded through Vite's `?worker` import. |
| Shared worker | `@livestore/adapter-web/shared-worker?sharedworker` | Coordinates the OPFS leader across tabs and iframes of the same origin. |
| `VectorCanvas` | `src/components/VectorCanvas.tsx` | Canvas 2D rendering (`cad/renderer.ts`), hit testing and translation (`cad/geometry.ts`), redraw on `doc.$` via `requestAnimationFrame`, ghost rendering while `doc.isTentative`. |
| `PropertyInspector` | `src/components/PropertyInspector.tsx` | MobX `observer` form for the selected shape (name, layer, fill, stroke, stroke width, rotation, bounding box); the name input is buffered and debounced by 200 ms. |
| `SplitSimulator` | `src/components/SplitSimulator.tsx` | Viewport modes, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z hotkeys, export and import of `.cad` files. |
| `TelemetryMonitor` | `src/components/TelemetryMonitor.tsx` | Classifies events into `ephemeral`, `sqlite`, `cdc`; throughput, disk-write and per-category counters; channel filters; simulation buttons. |
| Telemetry helpers | `src/telemetry/types.ts` | `calculateThroughput`, `filterTelemetryEvents`, `extractUpdatedFields`, `calculatePayloadSize`. |
| Export / import | `src/cad/exportImport.ts` | Hand-built two-page SQLite 3 file (`cad_documents(id, title, data)`) and a parser that also accepts JSON payloads. |
| LiveStore spike | `src/components/LiveStoreSpikeHarness.tsx`, `src/livestore/schema.ts` | Raw LiveStore benchmark (`?spike=livestore`): host plus two iframes on `storeId: 'spike-livestore-cad'`, 100-commit latency run. |

### 2.1. Entry modes

| URL | Renders |
|---|---|
| `/` | Host shell: `SplitSimulator` in `single` mode plus `TelemetryMonitor`. |
| `/?split=dual` | Host shell starting in dual iframe mode. |
| `/?viewport=A`, `/?viewport=B` | Child viewport (canvas + inspector + undo/redo buttons) used inside the dual iframes. |
| `/?viewport=native` | Same child viewport opened in a real browser tab by the "native tab" mode. |
| `/?spike=livestore` | `LiveStoreSpikeHarness` instead of the CAD app. |

## 3. Data Flow

### 3.1. RAM streaming vs SQLite commits

A canvas drag never writes to SQLite per pointer event. `VectorCanvas` calls `store.doc.patch()` on every `pointermove`; livestruct applies the patch in memory, broadcasts it as a tentative overlay and coalesces it in its commit scheduler. `pointerup` calls `doc.flush()`, which commits the pending patch. The test suite pins this: 300 scripted moves at 8 ms intervals produce at most 4 commits.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Pointer
    participant C as VectorCanvas
    participant D as LiveDocument (doc-default)
    participant O as Overlay channel (BroadcastChannel)
    participant W as LiveStore worker (SQLite OPFS)
    U->>C: pointermove (60 fps)
    C->>D: doc.patch({ shapes: { id: { x, y } } })
    D-->>C: doc.$ emits (redraw on next frame)
    D->>O: tentative overlay (overlay_sent)
    U->>C: pointerup
    C->>D: doc.flush()
    D->>W: one committed patch (commit event)
    W-->>O: remote_commit to peers, overlays dropped
```

Inspector edits, selection changes, undo/redo and import go through `CadStore` methods or helpers that call `doc.patch()` followed by `await doc.flush()`, so each is one commit.

The msgmesh bus (`createMsgBus<CadMsgStruct>()`) carries the typed channel `cad.cursor.drag`. The monitor subscribes to it and classifies its messages as RAM traffic; the canvas itself drives drags through `doc.patch`, so this channel is an integration point for code that publishes drag streams, not the drag path.

### 3.2. Worker and shared-worker topology

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph TabOrIframe["Each tab / iframe (own JS heap)"]
        APP["App + CadStore"]
        LS["@actdim/livestruct store (sessionId per context)"]
        APP --> LS
    end
    LS -->|"?worker import"| DW["Dedicated worker: src/livestore/worker.ts"]
    LS -->|"?sharedworker import"| SW["Shared worker: @livestore/adapter-web"]
    DW --> DB[("SQLite in OPFS")]
    SW --- DW
    LS <-->|"livestruct:storeId:overlay"| BC(("BroadcastChannel"))
```

`initCadStore` imports both workers only in a browser and only when `forceMemory` is false. In Node (Vitest) `forceMemory` defaults to true and the store runs in memory; if the worker imports fail, `createLiveStruct` receives no workers.

### 3.3. Multi-tab sync

Every context (host, iframe A, iframe B, native tab) creates its own `CadStore` with a distinct `sessionId` (`session_<senderId>_<time>_<random>`) against the same store name. Peers receive tentative overlays first (the canvas renders ghost shapes and shows "Tentative Remote Overlay"), then the committed change, which livestruct reports as `remote_commit` and the monitor lists as `cdc.replica`. The dual iframes use `sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms'`, so they share the origin, OPFS and BroadcastChannel but no in-memory state.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Viewport A: doc.patch + flush"] --> SQL[("Shared SQLite (OPFS)")]
    A -.->|tentative overlay| B["Viewport B: ghost render"]
    SQL -->|remote_commit| B2["Viewport B: doc.$ emits committed data"]
    SQL -->|remote_commit| H["Host shell / native tab"]
```

### 3.4. Undo/redo

`CadStore` keeps per-context snapshot stacks. `commitShapeTransform` and `updateShapeProperties` push a deep copy of `doc.data` (stack capped at 50) and clear the redo stack; `selectShape` does not. `undo` / `redo` swap snapshots and call `applySnapshot`, which builds a patch that sets `title`, `selectedShapeId` and every shape of the target, and sets shapes missing from the target to `null`. Because the result is an ordinary committed patch, it replicates to other viewports like any edit; the stacks themselves stay local to the context that made the edits. Canvas drags patch the document directly and do not push undo snapshots.

### 3.5. Export and import

- **Export** (`exportCadDatabase`, `downloadCadProject`): serializes the current `doc.data` into a two-page SQLite 3 file built byte by byte (`CREATE TABLE cad_documents (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, data TEXT)`, one row whose `data` column is the document JSON; 4096-byte pages, 65536 when the row does not fit). It is downloaded as `project.cad` with type `application/x-sqlite3`. It does not copy the LiveStore OPFS database file.
- **Import** (`parseCadDatabase`, `importCadDatabase`): accepts that SQLite layout (with a JSON scan fallback), a LiveStruct JSON export (`documents["cad_documents:doc-default"].data`) or a raw `CadDocument` JSON. The parsed document is applied as one replacing patch plus `flush`, so all peers update; unknown formats throw `Unsupported or corrupted CAD project format.`

## 4. Invariants

1. **One store per browsing context**: `App` creates and closes the `CadStore` in an effect keyed by `viewport`; disposal closes the LiveStruct store and the events subscription.
2. **Drags commit once**: pointer moves only `doc.patch`; `pointerup` flushes. No component writes SQLite per frame.
3. **Every inspector, undo/redo and import edit is a committed patch**: these paths end with `await doc.flush()`.
4. **Peers sync only through the store**: iframes and tabs exchange data via OPFS/LiveStore and the livestruct overlay channel, never through `postMessage` (the spike harness uses `postMessage` only for benchmark reporting).
5. **Node tests stay in memory**: `forceMemory` defaults to true outside a browser; no worker or OPFS is touched by Vitest.
6. **Library behaviour lives in the libraries**: commit timing, overlay TTL and echo handling are livestruct settings; the demo does not reimplement them.
7. **Deployment path is configurable**: `vite.config.ts` uses `base: process.env.DEMO_BASE || '/'`; links inside the app are relative (`?viewport=A`) so they work under `/livestruct/demo/`.

## 5. Cross-Links

- [Domain Model](./topic--domain-model.md): shape and document model, channels, schemas, telemetry records.
- [Setup & Workflow](./topic--setup-and-workflow.md): commands, tests, browser requirements, Pages CI.
- [README](../README.md): scenarios and zone layout.

## Document: docs/topic--domain-model.md (Domain Model & Entity Ecosystem)

# @actdim/livestruct-demo Domain Model

## 1. Entity Taxonomy

| Entity | Defined in | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CadShape` | `src/cad/types.ts` | One drawing primitive: `rect`, `circle` or `line`. |
| `CadDocument` | `src/cad/types.ts` | The edited document: title, selection and a map of shapes. Stored as a LiveStruct document. |
| `CadStore` | `src/cad/store.ts` | Per-context facade: LiveStruct store, `cad_documents` collection, `doc-default` document, msgmesh bus, counters, undo/redo stacks. |
| `CursorDragPayload` | `src/cad/types.ts` | Message payload of the bus channel `cad.cursor.drag`. |
| `TelemetryEvent` | `src/telemetry/types.ts` | One row of the protocol monitor. |
| `TelemetryMetrics` | `src/telemetry/types.ts` | Aggregates shown in the monitor's metrics bar. |
| `.cad` project file | `src/cad/exportImport.ts` | Portable SQLite 3 file with one `cad_documents` row. |
| `docs` row (spike) | `src/livestore/schema.ts` | Raw LiveStore table used only by the `?spike=livestore` harness. |
| `BoundingBox`, `TransformHandle` | `src/cad/types.ts` | Derived geometry for hit testing and selection rendering (`src/cad/geometry.ts`). |

## 2. Front-matter Schemas

The demo has no Markdown entities of its own; its "records" are TypeScript and storage schemas.

### 2.1. CAD shape

```typescript
export type CadShapeType = 'rect' | 'circle' | 'line';

export interface CadShape {
    id: string;
    type: CadShapeType;
    x: number;
    y: number;
    width?: number;   // rect
    height?: number;  // rect
    radius?: number;  // circle
    x2?: number;      // line end
    y2?: number;      // line end
    name?: string;
    layer?: string;   // inspector default: 'geometry'
    fill?: string;
    stroke?: string;
    strokeWidth?: number;
    rotation?: number;
}
```

### 2.2. CAD document

```typescript
export interface CadDocument {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    selectedShapeId?: string | null;
    shapes: Record<string, CadShape>;
    activeLayer?: string;
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

`initCadStore` creates the document once per store if it is missing:

| Field | Seed value |
|---|---|
| collection | `cad_documents` |
| document id | `doc-default` |
| `title` | `Mechanical Assembly` |
| `selectedShapeId` | `rect-1` |
| `shapes` | `DEFAULT_SHAPES` or `options.initialShapes` |

`DEFAULT_SHAPES`:

| id | type | name | geometry |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rect-1` | `rect` | Main Bracket | x 60, y 60, 140 x 90 |
| `circle-1` | `circle` | Bearing Mount | x 320, y 120, radius 45 |
| `line-1` | `line` | Center Axis | (60, 240) -> (360, 240) |

All mutations are partial deep patches of `CadDocument`; a shape key set to `null` removes that shape (used by undo/redo and import).

### 2.3. Bus channels and payloads

The bus is `createMsgBus<CadMsgStruct>()` from `@actdim/msgmesh/core` (or `options.bus`).

```typescript
export interface CursorDragPayload {
    shapeId: string;
    x: number;
    y: number;
    dx: number;
    dy: number;
    timestamp: number;
    senderId?: string;
}

export type CadMsgStruct = {
    'cad.cursor.drag': { in: CursorDragPayload };
};

export const CAD_DRAG_CHANNEL = 'cad.cursor.drag' as const;
```

`TelemetryMonitor` listens on `CAD_DRAG_CHANNEL` with an abort signal and records each message as an `ephemeral` event, computing latency from `payload.timestamp`. Channel semantics (groups, request/response) are described on the msgmesh and msgmesh-store sites ([https://actdim.github.io/msgmesh-store/](https://actdim.github.io/msgmesh-store/)).

### 2.4. LiveStore schema usage

- **CAD app**: `src/livestore/worker.ts` runs `makeWorker({ schema })` with the schema from `@actdim/livestruct/engine`. The demo does not define tables for the CAD document; it uses the LiveStruct collection API (`liveStore.collection<CadDocument>('cad_documents')`, `collection.get`, `collection.create`, `doc.patch`, `doc.flush`, `doc.$`, `doc.isTentative`). Storage layout is described at [https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/](https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/).
- **Spike harness**: `src/livestore/schema.ts` defines a standalone LiveStore schema used with `makePersistedAdapter` and `storeId: 'spike-livestore-cad'`:

| Element | Definition |
|---|---|
| table `docs` | `id` text primary key, `body` text JSON (default `{}`), `mutation_id` text, `origin` text |
| event `doc.created` | `{ id, body, mutationId, origin }` -> insert row |
| event `doc.patched` | `{ id, patch, mutationId, origin }` -> `UPDATE docs SET body = json_patch(body, ?) ...` |
| event `doc.deleted` | `{ id, mutationId, origin }` -> delete row |

### 2.5. `.cad` project file

```sql
CREATE TABLE cad_documents (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, data TEXT)
```

One row: `id` = document id (default `doc-default`), `title`, `data` = `JSON.stringify(CadDocument)`. Import also accepts `{ "documents": { "cad_documents:doc-default": { "data": CadDocument } } }` and a bare `CadDocument` JSON object.

### 2.6. Telemetry messages

```typescript
export type TelemetryCategory = 'ephemeral' | 'sqlite' | 'cdc';

export interface TelemetryEvent {
    id: string;
    timestamp: number;
    category: TelemetryCategory;
    channel: string;
    latencyUs?: number;
    sizeBytes?: number;
    updatedFields?: string[];
    rev?: number;
    origin?: string;
    payloadSummary: string;
    rawPayload?: unknown;
}
```

Mapping from sources to monitor rows:

| Source | Channel | Category | Badge |
|---|---|---|---|
| LiveStruct `local_patch` | `livestruct.patch` | `ephemeral` | RAM |
| LiveStruct `overlay_sent` | `livestruct.overlay.sent` | `ephemeral` | RAM |
| LiveStruct `overlay_received` | `livestruct.overlay.received` | `cdc` | CDC |
| LiveStruct `commit` | `sqlite.commit` | `sqlite` | SQLITE COMMIT (with `rev`, size, fields) |
| LiveStruct `remote_commit` | `cdc.replica` | `cdc` | CDC REPLICA (with origin) |
| Bus `cad.cursor.drag` | `cad.cursor.drag` | `ephemeral` | RAM |
| "Simulate CDC" button | `cdc.replica` (origin `tab-2`) | `cdc` | CDC REPLICA |

`updatedFields` are leaf dot paths from `extractUpdatedFields(patch)` (for example `shapes.rect-1.x`); `sizeBytes` is the UTF-8 JSON size from `calculatePayloadSize`. `TelemetryMetrics` holds `messagesPerSec` (rolling 1 s window from `calculateThroughput`), `diskWriteCount` (from `CadStore.diskCommitCount` when a store exists), and per-category totals. Filters accept `ALL`, `cad.*`, `sqlite.*`, `cdc.*` or free text matched against channel, category, payload summary, origin and fields.

## 3. Graph Relationships

```mermaid
erDiagram
    CadStore ||--|| LiveStoreInstance : wraps
    CadStore ||--|| MsgBus : owns
    LiveStoreInstance ||--o{ LiveCollection : "collection('cad_documents')"
    LiveCollection ||--|| CadDocument : "doc-default"
    CadDocument ||--o{ CadShape : "shapes[id]"
    CadShape ||--|| BoundingBox : "getBoundingBox"
    MsgBus ||--o{ CursorDragPayload : "cad.cursor.drag"
    LiveStoreInstance ||--o{ TelemetryEvent : "events$ mapped"
    MsgBus ||--o{ TelemetryEvent : "drag messages mapped"
    CadDocument ||--|| CadProjectFile : "export / import"
```

- `CadDocument.selectedShapeId` references a key of `CadDocument.shapes` or is `null`.
- Each browsing context owns one `CadStore`; all contexts of one origin share the persisted `cad_documents/doc-default` through LiveStore.
- Undo/redo stacks hold whole `CadDocument` snapshots and are not persisted.

## 4. Cross-Links

- [Architecture](./topic--architecture.md): data flow, worker topology, invariants.
- [Setup & Workflow](./topic--setup-and-workflow.md): commands and tests that exercise these models.

## Document: docs/topic--setup-and-workflow.md (Setup, Build & Workflow)

# @actdim/livestruct-demo Setup, Build & Workflow

## 1. Prerequisites

- **Node.js**: 22 (the version the Pages workflow uses).
- **Package manager**: `pnpm` (CI pins 10.30.3).
- **Workspace**: the demo lives in `demo/` of the livestruct repository. It depends on `@actdim/livestruct` as `workspace:*`, declares `catalog:` versions for `@livestore/livestore`, `@livestore/adapter-web`, `@livestore/wa-sqlite` and `effect`, and `>=1.12.0` ranges for `@actdim/msgmesh` and `@actdim/utico`. It installs inside a pnpm workspace that provides that catalog: the livestruct repository root (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` with packages `.` and `demo`, the other `@actdim` packages from npm) or the mempart monorepo (`src/pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists `packages/livestruct/demo`, all `@actdim` packages from their folders).
- **Browser** (persistent mode): a secure context (`localhost` or HTTPS) with OPFS (`navigator.storage.getDirectory`), module `Worker`, `SharedWorker` and `BroadcastChannel`. A browser without `SharedWorker` cannot run the persisted multi-tab setup. Same-origin iframes need storage access, so private or third-party-cookie-restricted modes can block the dual view.

## 2. Running Inside mempart

The demo is the folder `src/packages/livestruct/demo` (inside the livestruct submodule) and a member of the mempart pnpm workspace; the nested `pnpm-workspace.yaml` of livestruct is ignored there. mempart's `src/package.json` has `dev:demo` / `build:demo` shortcuts only for `@actdim/dynstruct-demo`, so address this package with a filter from `src/`:

```bash
cd src
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo dev     # Vite dev server on http://localhost:4173
pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo build
pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo test
```

The workspace links `@actdim/livestruct`, `msgmesh` and `utico` from their sibling folders (the demo does not depend on `dynstruct` or `msgmesh-store`). Their `exports` point at `dist/`, so build a library (`pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct build`) after changing it before the demo sees the change.

Useful URLs on the dev server: `/` (host shell), `/?split=dual` (two isolated iframes), `/?viewport=A` (single child viewport), `/?spike=livestore` (raw LiveStore benchmark). In the browser console `window.__cadStore` is the active `CadStore`.

## 3. Runner Commands

Run from the package folder (or with `pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo <script>` from mempart `src/`).

| Command | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm run dev` | `vite` | Dev server on port 4173 with the dedicated LiveStore worker and shared worker. |
| `pnpm run build` | `tsc -b tsconfig.json && vite build` | Typechecks, then bundles the SPA into `dist/` (base path from `DEMO_BASE`, default `/`). |
| `pnpm run preview` | `vite preview` | Serves the built `dist/`. |
| `pnpm run test` | `npx vitest --config=vitest.node.config.ts --no-cache` | Runs `tests/**/*.test.ts` once in Node. |
| `pnpm run typecheck` | `tsc -b tsconfig.json` | Type checks without bundling. |
| `pnpm run format` | `prettier --write .` | Formats the package. |
| `pnpm run format:check` | `prettier --check .` | Verifies formatting. |

The Along test runner `.along/scripts/test.py` calls `pnpm test`.

## 4. Tests

`vitest.node.config.ts` runs in the `node` environment with globals, `pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: false`, setup file `vitest.setup.ts` (defines `globalThis.self`) and typecheck config `tsconfig.dev.json`. In Node `initCadStore` defaults to `forceMemory`, so no OPFS or worker is used.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `tests/vectorCanvas.test.ts` | Geometry (bounding boxes, hit testing, translation, handles), drag patches without synchronous writes, one commit on flush, 300-move drag benchmark with at most 4 commits, reaction to external `doc.$` updates, renderer routines. |
| `tests/propertyInspector.test.ts` | MobX observer rendering, per-field patch commits, canvas-to-inspector sync, shape selector, 200 ms name debounce and flush. |
| `tests/splitSimulator.test.ts` | Cross-viewport overlays and commits, echo suppression, mode switching and iframe sandbox, undo/redo replication, `.cad` export as valid SQLite, import of SQLite and JSON payloads with peer propagation. |
| `tests/telemetryMonitor.test.ts` | Badges per category, throughput metrics, channel and text filters, field and size extraction, live `CadStore` event capture, simulation controls. |

## 5. GitHub Pages CI

The livestruct repository workflow `.github/workflows/pages.yml` publishes one site: the docs at [https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/](https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/) and the demo at [https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/demo/](https://actdim.github.io/livestruct/demo/). It runs on push to `main` (docs, `src/`, `demo/`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the workflow) and on manual dispatch.

After the docs build, the `Build demo` step (with `DEMO_BASE=<base_path>/demo/`):

1. Runs `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` in the repository workspace (`.` and `demo`; the catalog lives in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`).
2. Builds the library (`pnpm run build`), because the demo imports `@actdim/livestruct` through its `dist/` exports.
3. Builds the demo (`pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo build`) and copies `demo/dist` to `.dist-docs/demo`.

`@actdim/msgmesh` and `@actdim/utico` come from npm. Until they are published at `>=1.12.0` the step fails; it is `continue-on-error`, so the docs still deploy without the demo.

### 5.1. Local reproduction

From the livestruct repository root (bash, outside mempart):

```bash
pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
DEMO_BASE=/livestruct/demo/ pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo build
pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo preview -- --base /livestruct/demo/
```

PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:DEMO_BASE = '/livestruct/demo/'; pnpm --filter @actdim/livestruct-demo build
```

## 6. Quality Gates

1. `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run test` pass (the Along test gate runs `pnpm test`).
2. `pnpm run format:check` is clean.
3. `pnpm run build` succeeds with and without `DEMO_BASE`; relative links (`?viewport=A`) keep working under `/livestruct/demo/`.
4. A manual check in a browser with OPFS: drag a shape in `/?split=dual`, confirm the peer shows the tentative ghost and then the committed position, and that the monitor shows one `sqlite.commit` per drag.
5. Commit-time `along lint`: ASCII text, fenced code with languages, relative links.
6. Versioning: the package version follows the mempart monorepo. Change it only with `pnpm run version:sync <version>` from mempart `src/`, never by editing this `package.json` alone.
